quandoUsar: Small quantities with known limits, adjusted one step at a time: guests, nights, cart items.
Form or list rows where the control cannot change width: the space for the two buttons and the largest value stays reserved even when a button disappears.
When the limit needs to be obvious: at `min` or `max` the matching button disappears, instead of just being dimmed.
quandoEvitar: Use `number-field` when the person needs to type the value: here the number is not editable, only the buttons and arrows change it.
Use `slider` for wide or continuous ranges, where reaching the value step by step would take too many taps.

teclado.acao: Adds one `step`.
Subtracts one `step`.
Adds or subtracts `largeStep` (by default, five steps).
Goes to `min` or to `max`.
Moves focus to the number; the minus and plus buttons are outside the tab order.

acessibilidade: The number is a `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax`; `label` is required and becomes the accessible name.
Pass `formatValueText` so the screen reader announces the value with a unit (“3 nights”) instead of the bare number.
Pressing a button moves focus to the number, so focus is not lost when the button disappears at the limit; the buttons have an English `aria-label` (`Increase …`, `Decrease …`), built from `label`.
movimento: Each digit rolls up when the value goes up and down when it goes down, with a spring with no overshoot and a slight blur.
At `min` or `max` the matching button folds against the edge and disappears, and the number slides half a button toward the side that became empty.
With “reduce motion” on, digits and buttons only fade and the number changes place instantly.
responsivo: The width is fixed (two buttons plus the digits of the larger of `min` and `max`) and the height follows `size`: 36, 44, or 50 px.
notasIA: Works controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`, which falls back to `min`); the defaults are `min={0}`, `max={10}`, and `step={1}`.
`label` is required and does not show on screen: put the visible text alongside, and pass `name` if the value should go along on form submission (it becomes a hidden field).
Holding a button already repeats the step (waits 380 ms, then one every 75 ms) and the decimal places follow those of `step` and `min`: do not reimplement this externally.

quandoUsar: Single choice among text options where the rotating gesture is part of the experience: camera lens, mode, period.
Touch screens or ones with a mouse wheel, where dragging along the arc or scrolling is more direct than opening a menu.
Ordered sets where seeing the current option and its neighbors is enough: labels fade with distance and disappear a little over three positions from the apex.
quandoEvitar: Use `segmented-control` when there are few options and all need to be visible at the same time.
Use `wheel-picker` for vertical reels of time or date, with several columns.
Use `select` in dense forms: the horizontal arc takes 30rem by 8rem by default.

teclado.acao: Rotates to the next enabled option.
Rotates to the previous enabled option.
Goes to the first or last enabled option.

acessibilidade: The root is a focusable `role="listbox"` with `aria-activedescendant` pointing to the chosen option; each label is a `role="option"` with `aria-selected`.
`label` is required and becomes the `aria-label`; `aria-orientation` becomes `vertical` on the `left` and `right` arcs.
Options with `disabled` appear struck through, get `aria-disabled`, and the disc never stops on them, whether by key, wheel, click, or drag.
movimento: The disc rotates to the option with a gentle spring and, on releasing a drag, inherits the gesture's velocity before settling on the nearest enabled option.
The apex brackets adjust with a spring to the width of the nearest label, and labels shrink and fade as they move away.
Beyond the ends the drag offers elastic resistance; with “reduce motion” on, disc and brackets jump straight to the final position.
responsivo: The `top` or `bottom` arc measures 30rem by 8rem (variables `--span` and `--depth`, adjustable via `style`) and respects `max-width: 100%`; the ends fade out through a mask.
On touch, the horizontal arc lets the page scroll vertically (`touch-action: pan-y`) and the side arcs, horizontally.
desempenho: Label widths are measured in layout and again when fonts load, and each option tracks the disc position on every frame: keep the list short.
notasIA: `options` is `{ value, label?, disabled? }[]` with a unique `value`, and the component's `label` is required; use `value` + `onValueChange` or `defaultValue` (without it, the first enabled option applies).
`side` chooses the disc face (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`), a larger `radius` makes the arc flatter, and `gap` fixes the distance between options, which by default follows each label's width.
Over the component, the mouse wheel rotates the disc instead of scrolling the page (scrolling only returns at the ends): do not put it in the way of a long scroll.

quandoUsar: Pricing page where the billing period (monthly or yearly) changes the values shown on the plans.
When the cheaper option carries a savings badge whose text changes when it is chosen (`badge` → `activeBadge`).
Prices that should roll to the new value without pushing what is next to them: use `BillingPrice`, exported by the same file.
quandoEvitar: Use `segmented-control` to toggle views or filters that are not a billing period and carry no badge.
Use `switch` for an on or off setting with immediate effect.
Use `plan-comparison` when you need the full plan comparison, not just the period selector.

teclado.acao: Selects the next option and moves focus to it; from the last it wraps to the first.
Selects the previous option; from the first it goes to the last.
Selects the first or last option.
Enters the group at the selected option and leaves it; the other options are outside the tab order.

acessibilidade: The group is a `role="radiogroup"` and each option a `<button role="radio">` with `aria-checked` and a roving tabindex.
`label` names the group and defaults to English (`Billing period`): pass the text in the page language.

The badge is part of the option name, so the screen reader announces label and badge together; in `BillingPrice` the old price comes out in a `<del>` and the current value has a text copy for screen readers.
movimento: A single thumb slides between options with a spring with no overshoot, taking the position and width of the chosen option.
The badge swaps text in place, in a box that already has the width of the longest text; in `BillingPrice` the digits roll to the new value and the old price (`was`) opens in width.
With “reduce motion” on, the thumb and digits jump into place and texts only fade.
responsivo: Labels and badges do not wrap (`white-space: nowrap`): on narrow screens, keep the texts short.
`BillingPrice` pushes the period to the line below when width runs short (`flex-wrap`).
notasIA: It is always controlled: `value` and `onValueChange` are required; without `options` it shows `Monthly` and `Yearly` with the `Save 20%` badge, in English.
The file also exports `BillingPrice` (`amount`, `currency`, `period`, `was`, `decimals`); `was` only shows struck through when it is greater than `amount`.
Depends on `animated-counter`; the active badge color comes from `--billing-accent` (default `--success`), which can be defined on any ancestor.

quandoUsar: Choosing a single day with the month always visible on the page: scheduling, delivery, an agenda side panel.
When some days cannot be chosen: `minDate`, `maxDate`, and the `disabledDates` function block days, and the keyboard skips over them.
As a piece of your own picker: `month` and `onMonthChange` control the visible month, as `date-picker` does.
quandoEvitar: Use `date-picker` when the calendar should open from a form field and close after the choice.
Use `date-range-picker` to choose a start and end: this calendar holds a single day.
Use `activity-heatmap` to display values per day across the year; this calendar is for choosing a date, not for visualizing data.

teclado.acao: Moves focus one day back or forward, skipping blocked days.
Moves focus one week back or forward.
Goes to the Sunday or Saturday of the focused week.
Goes to the same day of the previous or next month, and the visible month follows.
Goes back or forward one year.
Selects the focused day.

acessibilidade: Each month is a `role="grid"` and each day a button with the full-text date in `aria-label`, `aria-selected`, and, on today, `aria-current="date"`.
Only one day is in the tab order (the last focused, the selected, today, or the first available), and the month change is announced by an `aria-live` region.
`locale` translates the month, the weekdays, and the date read out on each day, but `Today`, `Previous month`, and `Next month` are fixed English texts.
movimento: Months sit side by side in a strip that slides with a spring with no overshoot; quick clicks redirect the same spring instead of queuing animations.
The selection disc slides in a straight line from one day to another, and each number changes color the moment the disc passes over it.
With “reduce motion” on, month, title, and disc swap in place, with no displacement.
responsivo: Takes `min(100%, 328px)` and every grid has six weeks, so the height does not change from one month to another.
The header is its own container: below 260 px of width the title takes a full line and the controls drop to the next line.
desempenho: Only the destination month and those still passing through the strip stay mounted, with 42 buttons each; the month leaving becomes `inert`.
notasIA: Selection is always controlled: keep the date in state and pass `value` and `onChange`, otherwise no day is marked; the visible month can be left to the component or come from `month`.
The week always starts on Sunday and `locale` defaults to `en-US`: pass `locale="pt-BR"` to get the names in Portuguese.
Without `value` or `month`, the grid is only filled after hydration, because “today” comes from the visitor's clock (`useToday`).

quandoUsar: Independent options that can be checked in any combination, like notification preferences.
Explicit acceptance in a form (terms, consent), which only counts on submit.
A “select all” box that summarizes a group: `checked="indeterminate"` shows the dash when only some of the items are checked.
quandoEvitar: Use `switch` when the change takes effect immediately, with no save button.
Use `radio-group` when only one option can be checked.
Use `chip-group` for filters people turn on and off often above a list.

teclado.acao: Checks or unchecks the focused box; `Enter` does not toggle.

acessibilidade: Uses Radix's `Checkbox`: a button with `role="checkbox"` and `aria-checked`, which is `mixed` in the indeterminate state.
`label` generates a `<label>` tied to the control and `description` goes in via `aria-describedby`; without `label`, pass `aria-label`, otherwise the accessible name becomes the generic `Checkbox`.
The click area is 44 px on a side, although the drawn square is 18 px, and clicking the label also toggles.
movimento: The fill grows on a short spring while the checkmark stroke draws itself; on uncheck, the stroke retracts.
The checkmark and the indeterminate dash have the same three points, so one transforms into the other instead of swapping.
With “reduce motion” on, the state change is instant and the square does not shrink when pressed.
notasIA: Controlled with `checked` + `onCheckedChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultChecked`; the value can be `true`, `false`, or `"indeterminate"`.
In `onCheckedChange`, compare with `=== true` before storing a boolean, because the received value can be `"indeterminate"`.
The other props go to Radix's `Checkbox.Root` (`disabled`, `required`, `name`, `value`) and the `ref` points to the button.

quandoUsar: Filtering a list by a few facets people turn on and off often: topics, status, tags.
Longer sets where only the first ones need to appear: `maxVisible` collapses the rest behind a “+N more” chip and keeps the selected ones in view.
Single choice that can be empty: with `multiple={false}`, clicking the checked chip clears the selection.
quandoEvitar: Use `segmented-control` when exactly one option must always be selected.
Use `multi-select` when the options should stay collapsed inside a form field, with label and description.
Use `tag-input` when the values are typed by the person, not chosen from a fixed set.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the next chip; from the last it wraps to the first.
Moves focus to the previous chip; from the first it goes to the last.
Moves focus to the first or last chip.
Checks or unchecks the focused chip; on the overflow chip, shows or collapses the rest.
Enters and leaves the group through a single chip: the last focused, the first selected, or the first in the list.

acessibilidade: The group is a `role="group"` named by `label` (required) and each chip is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed`; the arrows only move focus, they do not change the selection.
The overflow chip exposes `aria-expanded`, but its `+N more` and `Show less` texts are fixed in English.
The checked state does not depend on color alone: besides the tone, a checkmark sign enters before the label.
movimento: On check, the checkmark grows and draws itself in the space the label opens by sliding, and the chip border follows with a spring.
Neighboring chips slide to the new place, even when changing lines, and the group height follows with a spring when the number of lines changes.
With “reduce motion” on, widths and positions swap instantly and revealed chips only fade.
responsivo: Chips wrap (`flex-wrap`) and a label wider than the container is cut with an ellipsis.
desempenho: Each chip keeps a `ResizeObserver` and a layout animation, and the group another observer for the height: it suits a few facets, and `maxVisible` avoids mounting dozens of chips at once.
notasIA: It is always controlled and `value` is always an array, even with `multiple={false}` (one item or empty); `label` is required.
`options` is `{ value, label }[]` with a unique `value`; in multiple mode the returned array follows the order of `options`, not the order of clicks.
With `maxVisible`, selected chips stay in view on collapse, so the “+N” counts only those that were hidden.

quandoUsar: Free color choice in a theme, brand, or label editor, with opacity and text input in hex, RGB, HSL, or OKLCH.
When legibility matters: `background` feeds the WCAG contrast reading (ratio and level) of the color over the background it will sit on.
Flows where people save and reuse colors: saved swatches can be applied, reordered, and removed.
quandoEvitar: Use `color-swatches` when the choice is among a few fixed colors, like a product's finishes.
Avoid inside containers that clip content or near the right or bottom edge of the screen: the panel uses no portal and does not flip, it grows down and to the right from the swatch.
When the color needs to be confirmed or canceled: each adjustment calls `onValueChange` right away and the done button only closes the panel.

teclado.acao: Open and close the panel from the swatch and apply the focused saved color; in the text field, `Enter` applies the typed value.
Move the focused control by 1: saturation and brightness in the area, hue and opacity on the bars; among saved colors, `←` and `→` move focus.
Take steps of 10 instead of 1 on the color controls.
On the hue and opacity bars, go to the minimum or maximum; on saved colors, to the first or last.
Change the position of the focused saved color; `Delete` or `Backspace` remove it.
Closes the panel and returns focus to the swatch; with a value being edited in the text field, it first discards what was typed.

acessibilidade: The swatch is a button with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; the panel is a non-modal `role="dialog"`, with no focus trap, and does not close if focus leaves it with `Tab`.
On open, focus goes to the saturation and brightness control; `Esc` and the done button return focus to the swatch.
The controls are `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` and the contrast has a text version for screen readers, but the internal labels (`Hue`, `Opacity`, `Done`…) are fixed in English.
movimento: The swatch grows into the panel through an animated clip with a spring, and the content appears just behind the advancing edge.
Controls follow the pointer with a short spring, the format button morphs the text from one format into the other, and an invalid value makes the field shake.
With “reduce motion” on, the panel only fades, controls jump to position, and the text switches format with no transition.
responsivo: The panel is `min(19rem, 100vw - 32px)` wide and opens over the swatch, growing down and to the right: reserve that space in the layout.
desempenho: The panel is only mounted while it is open or closing, and the eyedropper only appears where the browser offers the `EyeDropper` API.
notasIA: `value` accepts hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, or `oklch()`, but `onValueChange` always returns uppercase hex, with two alpha digits when the color is not opaque.

Color and swatches work controlled or not: `value` or `defaultValue`, and `swatches` or `defaultSwatches` with `onSwatchesChange`; when saving beyond `maxSwatches` (default 7), the last one in the list drops out.
Depends on `text-morph`, and the file also exports `parseColor` and `toHex` to convert colors outside the component.

quandoUsar: Choosing one of a few fixed colors: a product finish, the color of a label or a project.
When some color may be unavailable: `disabled` on the option shows it struck through, and the keyboard skips over it.
In forms: `name` adds a hidden field with the chosen value.
quandoEvitar: Use `color-picker` when the person needs any color, with hue, opacity, or a typed value.
Use `radio-cards` when each option needs visible text, price, or description; here the color name only appears in the mouse tooltip and for the screen reader.
To check several colors at the same time: it is a radio group, so only one is chosen.

teclado.acao: Chooses the next enabled color; from the last it wraps to the first.
Chooses the previous enabled color; from the first it goes to the last.
Chooses the first or last enabled color.
Chooses the focused color, when it is not already the chosen one.
Enters the group at the chosen color, or at the first enabled one when nothing has been chosen.

acessibilidade: The group is a `role="radiogroup"` named by `label` (required) and each color is a `role="radio"` button with `aria-checked` and a roving tabindex.
Give each option a `label`: it is the name read by the screen reader and the mouse tooltip; without it, what is heard is the `value`.
The choice is marked by an outer ring and the unavailable color by a strike, so neither state depends on color alone.
movimento: A single ring slides from one color to another with a gentle spring, instead of vanishing from one and appearing on the other.
The swatch grows slightly under the cursor and sinks when pressed.
With “reduce motion” on, the ring changes place instantly and swatches do not change scale.
responsivo: Swatches wrap (`flex-wrap`) and measure 24, 32, or 40 px depending on `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`).
notasIA: `options` is `{ value, color, label?, disabled? }[]`, and `color` accepts any CSS color, including tokens like `var(--tone-teal)`.
Controlled with `value` + `onValueChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`; the group's `label` is required and does not show on screen.
Since the color name is not visible, show the choice as text alongside, as the demo does with “Finish: Moss”; `shape` toggles between `circle` and `rounded`.

quandoUsar: Choosing a value from a list too long to scan without search: country, time zone, owner.
When people search for terms that are not in the label: each option's `keywords` go into the filter.
Form fields that need a visible label and help text: `label` and `description` already come tied to the field.
quandoEvitar: Use `select` for short lists, where typing does not help.
Use `multi-select` when the person can choose several values.
Use `command-palette` when the results are actions or destinations, not a field's value.

teclado.acao: Open the list if it is closed; when open, move the highlight through the enabled options, wrapping around at the ends.
Chooses the highlighted option, closes the list, and keeps focus in the field.
Closes the list and discards the typed text, keeping the previous selection.

acessibilidade: The field is a `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, and `aria-activedescendant`; focus stays in the field while the arrows move through the options.

`label` is required and becomes a visible `<label>`, `description` goes in via `aria-describedby`, and the empty-list message is a `role="status"`; the clear button has a fixed English name (`Clear selection`).
The list opens as soon as the field gets focus and does not close when leaving with `Tab`: only with `Esc`, a choice, or a click outside.
movimento: The list enters with a fade and a slight growth from the top, and its height follows the filter with a spring with no overshoot.
The chosen label settles into the field rising from a slight blur, the clear button grows as it appears, and the arrow rotates 180° with the list open.
With “reduce motion” on, only short fades remain and the height changes instantly.
responsivo: The list has the width of the field, always opens downward, and scrolls inside above `min(300px, 40vh)`; long labels are cut with an ellipsis.
It is positioned inside the component itself, with no portal: an ancestor with `overflow: hidden` clips it.
desempenho: All options that pass the filter are rendered, with no virtualization, and the list height is measured by a `ResizeObserver` on every filter change.
notasIA: Controlled with `value` + `onValueChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`; clearing the selection calls `onValueChange("")`.

The filter is local, by substring of `label` and `keywords`; it ignores case but not accents (`sao` does not find “São Paulo”) and the typed text is not exposed, so it does not work for server-side search.
Give each option a `value` with no spaces, because it goes into the `id` used by `aria-activedescendant`; the other props and the `ref` go to the `<input>`.

quandoUsar: A single date inside a form, with a label, help text, and the calendar opening under the field.
Dates with restrictions: `minDate`, `maxDate`, and `disabledDates` block days, like weekends on a delivery.
When the date can be left empty: the calendar footer has a clear button, which calls `onChange(undefined)`.
quandoEvitar: Use `date-range-picker` to choose the start and end of a period.
Use `calendar` when the month should always be visible on the page, with no field or popover.
For distant dates the person knows by heart, like a birth date: there is no typing, and the year only changes by keyboard or month by month.

teclado.acao: On the field, open the calendar and move focus to the selected day, to today, or to the first available day of the month.
In the calendar, move focus one day or one week, skipping blocked days.
Go to the Sunday or Saturday of the focused week.
Change month; with `Shift`, year.
On a day, choose the date and close the calendar.
Closes the calendar without changing the date and returns focus to the field.

acessibilidade: The field is a `<button>` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`, tied to the visible `label` and to `description`; the formatted value also goes in a screen-reader-only text.
On open, focus goes to a day in the calendar; on choosing a day or closing with `Esc`, it returns to the field, and leaving with `Tab` closes the popover.
The popover is a `role="dialog"` with no focus trap, and its texts (`Clear`, `Choose a day`, `Selected …`) are fixed in English, even with `locale`.
movimento: The calendar grows from the field's icon with a short spring and only closes 300 ms after the choice, so the highlight reaches the day.
In the field, only the parts of the date that changed roll: a later date rises from below, an earlier one drops from above.
With “reduce motion” on, everything becomes a fade and the calendar closes immediately after the choice.
responsivo: The popover is `min(320px, 100vw - 32px)`, always opens below the field, left-aligned, and on screens up to 360 px it takes the field's width.
There is no portal or flip upward: leave free space below the field and avoid ancestors with `overflow: hidden`.
notasIA: It is always controlled: keep `Date | undefined` in state and pass `value` and `onChange`; there is no `defaultValue`.
Pass `locale="pt-BR"` (the default is `en-US`) and, for another format in the field, `format` with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` options.
Depends on `calendar`; extra props and `disabled` go to the field's button, and `showToday` adds the today button to the header.

quandoUsar: A report period or dashboard filter, where shortcuts like “Last 7 days” solve most cases.
Bookings and searches where start and end are chosen together and only count after confirming with `Apply`.
Toolbars: closed, it takes only the width of its own text, and the panel grows over the page without pushing the content.
quandoEvitar: Use `date-picker` when one date is enough.
Use `calendar` when the month needs to stay open on the page.
When you need to block individual days, like holidays or weekends: there are only `minDate` and `maxDate`, with no function to disable dates.

teclado.acao: On the trigger, open the panel; on a day, mark the start and, the second time, the end of the period.
On days, move focus one day or one week; after the start is marked, the period stretches to the focused day.
Go to the first or last day of the week, according to `weekStartsOn`.
Change one month; with `Shift`, one year.
In the shortcut list, move from one shortcut to another: `↑` and `↓` in the wide panel, `←` and `→` in the compact one.
Closes without applying and returns focus to the trigger.

acessibilidade: The trigger has an `aria-label` with `label` and the current period; the panel is a `role="dialog"`, each month a `role="grid"`, and days inside the period get `aria-selected`.

An `aria-live` region announces the marked start and then the period with the day count; on open, focus goes to the period start or to today, and `Esc`, `Cancel`, and `Apply` return it to the trigger.
`label` does not show on screen, and `Cancel`, `Apply`, `Presets`, and the announcements are fixed in English; only the shortcut labels change, via the `presets` prop.
movimento: The trigger surface grows with a spring to the size of the panel and shrinks back; on apply, the period text flies from the footer to the trigger.
The highlight stretches week by week as the cursor or focus moves, the ends slide from one day to another, and the months enter from the navigation side.
With “reduce motion” on, sizes and positions jump to the end and the content only fades.
responsivo: With less than 712 px free in the boundary (the window or the `boundary` element), it shows a single month and shortcuts become a row with horizontal scrolling; `months` forces 1 or 2.
The panel shifts horizontally to fit the boundary with an 8 px margin and, on short screens, scrolls the page until the `Apply` button appears.
desempenho: The panel is only mounted while it is open; during that time there is a `ResizeObserver` on it and a `resize` listener on the window, in addition to the trigger's permanent observer.
notasIA: `onChange` only fires on `Apply`, never on each click; use `value` (with `null` for empty) or `defaultValue`, and remember the period includes both end days.
Pass `boundary={() => elemento}` when the picker lives in a panel or column: the panel stays inside it and the choice between one and two months uses that width.
Replace `presets` with Portuguese labels (`{ label, range: hoje => ({ start, end }) }`) and pass `locale="pt-BR"` and, if the week starts on Monday, `weekStartsOn={1}`.

quandoUsar: Continuous adjustments where the feel of the control matters, like volume, brightness, or intensity.
Values with reference points: `marks` creates stops where the thumb snaps when passing within 7 px of them, with clickable labels under the track.
When heavy work should only run at the end of the gesture: `onValueChange` follows the drag and `onValueCommit` fires on release or on each key.
quandoEvitar: Use `slider` for a range with two thumbs; this one has just one.
Use `number-field` when the exact value matters and needs to be typed.
Use `ruler-slider` to choose precisely on a long scale, with a ruler and inertia.

teclado.acao: Adds one `step`.
Subtracts one `step`.
Adds or subtracts `largeStep` (by default, a tenth of the range).
Move `largeStep` instead of `step`.
Goes to `min` or to `max`.

acessibilidade: The thumb is a focusable `role="slider"`, named by the visible `label`, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and an `aria-valuetext` that comes from `format`.
The value next to the label and the tag over the thumb are decorative (`aria-hidden`): what the screen reader announces is the `aria-valuetext`.
Clicking or tapping anywhere on the track moves focus to the thumb, and its touch area extends 12 px beyond the circle.
movimento: Past the ends the track stretches like a rubber band (up to 26 px), thins, and on release returns with a spring that overshoots and settles; on the keyboard, pushing against a limit gives the same jolt.
The value tag follows the thumb with a slight delay and sways with the velocity; on snapping to a mark, its dot pulses and, on touch, the device vibrates where supported.
With “reduce motion” on, there is no stretching or sway: the thumb jumps to the value and the tag only fades.
responsivo: Takes 100% of the container width and only exists horizontally; `--elastic-thumb` and `--elastic-track` adjust the sizes (default 24 px and 8 px).
On touch, dragging vertically still scrolls the page (`touch-action: pan-y`) and, on coarse pointers, the tag rises higher so it does not sit under the finger.
notasIA: `label` is required and visible; use `value` + `onValueChange` or `defaultValue` (which falls back to `min`), with defaults `min={0}`, `max={100}`, and `step={1}`.
The default number format is `en-US`: pass `format` for currency, unit, or Portuguese separators; it applies to the text next to the label, the tag, and the screen reader.
`marks` accepts numbers or `{ value, label }`, `startIcon` and `endIcon` put icons at the ends, and `name` sends the value in a hidden field.

quandoUsar: Headers and toolbars where an always-open search field would crowd the layout.
Searching a set that is already on the client (projects, documents, people), with results grouped by `group` right below the field.
When it is worth suggesting something before typing: `suggestions` appears as soon as the field opens, under the `suggestionsLabel` heading.
quandoEvitar: Use `search-field` when search is the screen's main action and should always be visible as a field.
Use `command-palette` when the results are commands with shortcuts, not items to open.
Use `morphing-search` when you need to control the text and the opening from outside or open the search with a keyboard shortcut: here the query and state are internal.

teclado.acao: On the magnifier button, open the field and move focus to it.
Move the highlight through the results or suggestions, wrapping around at the ends.
In the field, chooses the highlighted item, calls `onSelect`, and collapses the search.
Collapses the field back to the icon, clears the text, and returns focus to the button.

acessibilidade: Collapsed, it is a `<button>` named by `label`; open, the field is a `role="combobox"` with `aria-activedescendant`, and the results form a `role="listbox"` with labeled groups.
A `role="status"` region announces the number of results or the lack of them in fixed English (`3 results`, `No results for …`); `emptyHint` and `suggestionsLabel` are translatable via props.
When typing, the first result is already highlighted, so `Enter` chooses it; leaving the empty field collapses it, and the clear button stays outside the tab order.
movimento: The round button stretches into the field with a spring, and the corner radius follows the width, from circle to control radius.
The panel unfolds from the field and then only the height follows the content; rows slide to the new position when the list changes and the highlight travels from one row to another.
With “reduce motion” on, the width changes instantly and panel and results only fade.
responsivo: Takes 100% of the container width as a strip that does not intercept clicks; the field grows up to `expandedWidth` (default 360 px) or the width of that strip, whichever is smaller.
The results panel scrolls inside above `min(22rem, 60vh)`, and long titles are cut with an ellipsis.
desempenho: The search scans all of `items` on every key, but only `maxResults` rows (default 6) are rendered; two `ResizeObserver`s track the strip and the panel.
notasIA: Put it in a container with the width the field may take and choose `anchor` (`start` or `end`, default `end`) to say which edge the button sits on.
`label` is required; each item is `{ id, title, meta?, group?, icon?, keywords? }`, and the order of the groups follows the first appearance of each one in `items`.
The text and the open state are internal: react to `onSelect(item)` and `onExpandedChange`; the search is local, looks at `title`, `meta`, and `keywords`, and is case-insensitive.

quandoUsar: Attaching one or several files by dragging, picking from the device, or pasting a screenshot with the pointer over the target or focus inside it.
Uploads with per-file feedback: with `onUpload`, each row shows progress, completion, or failure, with a retry button.
When there are input rules: `accept`, `maxSize`, and `maxFiles` reject files with a message, and the target shakes slightly.
quandoEvitar: Use `file-upload` when the file list needs to be controlled from outside (`value` + `onChange`); here it is internal state and `defaultItems` only applies on mount.
Use `prompt-input` for attachments inside a message box, where they appear as chips.
To replace a single image, like a profile photo or cover, a button that opens the picker takes less space than the whole target.

teclado.acao: On the target, open the system file picker.
In the list, move focus to the row above or below, keeping the same action (remove or retry).
Remove the file in the focused row.
Moves through the target and each row's buttons.

acessibilidade: The whole target is a single `<button>` described by `description` and the note; the native `<input type="file">` stays hidden and outside the tab order.
Additions, completions, failures, and removals go out in a `role="status"` region, rejections in a `role="alert"`, and each upload has a `role="progressbar"`; these texts are fixed in English.
On removing a row, focus goes to the next row's remove button (or the previous one, or the target); on retry, to the same row's remove button.
movimento: With a file over the target, the dashed border closes into a solid line, the target pulses slowly, the icon's three sheets fan out, and a light on the border follows the pointer.
New rows drop from the target into the list in sequence and open their own height; the bar and the percentage follow the same spring and, on completion, a checkmark draws itself.
With “reduce motion” on, rows and texts only fade, progress jumps to the value, and there is no pulse or shake.
responsivo: The list is a query container: below 440 px the retry button keeps only the icon, and below 300 px the file's icon or thumbnail disappears.
`compactAt` folds the target into a low bar when the list reaches that number of files, and `listPlacement="inside"` puts the list inside the target's border.
desempenho: Added images get a thumbnail via `URL.createObjectURL`, released on removing the row or unmounting; at those same moments, in-progress uploads are aborted by the `signal`.
notasIA: `onUpload(item, { onProgress, signal })` must return a promise: report 0 to 100, resolve on completion, and reject with an `Error` whose message becomes the failure reason; respect the `signal`.
Without `onUpload` the list shows only the selections; `onFilesChange(files)` delivers the current `File`s, and the defaults are `multiple` on and `maxFiles={5}`.
`maxSize` is in bytes and `accept` takes extensions, MIME types, and wildcards like `image/*`; `label`, `description`, `note`, and `dropLabel` default to English.

quandoUsar: Names and short texts that are read far more than edited: project title, file name, description.
Editing that saves field by field, with no form: `onSave` can return a promise, and the new text appears right away while it runs.
Headings that need to stay headings: `as` keeps the text in an `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `p`, or `span`.
quandoEvitar: Use `input` or `textarea` in a form when several fields need to be saved together.
Use `rich-text-editor` when the text needs formatting.
When leaving the field must not save: here losing focus saves, as in a rename, and only `Esc` discards.

teclado.acao: On the text, enter edit mode with all the content selected.
In the field, saves; does not fire during an IME composition.
With `multiline`, inserts a line break.
Cancels the edit, restores the text, and returns focus to it.
Moves through the save and cancel buttons; when focus leaves the component, the text is saved.

acessibilidade: At rest the text is a `<button>` with an `aria-label` in the format “label: value” and the hint `Activate to edit.`; while editing it becomes an `<input>` or `<textarea>` with the same `label`.
The `validate` error is tied to the field by `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`, and the saving and saved notices go out in a `role="status"` region.
The hints, the announcements, and the failure message (with the `Try again` button) are fixed in English; only `label`, `placeholder`, and the `validate` text come from you.
movimento: The text becomes a field in the same place and with the same metrics; the frame follows the width of what is typed with a fast spring and, with `multiline`, the height.

On save, the new text stays dimmed next to a spinning indicator until the promise resolves, and then a checkmark draws itself; on failure, the saved text comes back and the frame flashes in an error tone.
With “reduce motion” on, sizes change instantly, texts only fade, and the saving indicator does not spin.
responsivo: The row reserves 66 px on the right for the buttons (38 px with `multiline`), so the text does not change wrapping on entering edit mode; on a single line, the excess is cut with an ellipsis.
notasIA: `value` is the saved value and `onSave(next)` must store it: return a promise and reject it for the component to restore the last saved value and offer a retry.
`validate(next)` returns the error message or nothing; before that the text is trimmed and, on a single line, repeated spaces become one, and `onSave` is not called if nothing changed.
`label` is required (it is the accessible name and does not show on screen), `variant` is `title` or `body`, and `as` chooses the tag, for example `as="h2"`.

quandoUsar: Single-line text in a form: name, email, URL, code.
Fields that need visible help and validation: `description` and `error` open their own line under the field without jolting the layout.
Messages with a count that changes while typing, like “12 characters left”: only the changed digits roll.
quandoEvitar: Use `textarea` for multi-line text.
Use `password-field` for passwords and `search-field` for search: they already bring the reveal and clear buttons.
Use `number-field` or `money-input` for numbers and money values, which need limits, steps, and formatting.
acessibilidade: It is a native `<input>` with a `<label>` tied by `htmlFor`; `label` is required.
`error` marks the field with `aria-invalid` and the message goes out in a `role="alert"`; `description` and `error` go into `aria-describedby`, added to whatever you pass in that prop.
Focus is indicated only by the border darkening, with no ring; the animated words of the messages are hidden, and the screen reader reads a plain-text copy.
movimento: The help and error lines open their own height with a spring, and the words rise from a slight blur.
When the message changes, only the different words move, and numbers roll up if they grew and down if they shrank.
With “reduce motion” on, the lines appear already at final size and the words only fade.
responsivo: Takes 100% of the container width, with a minimum height of 44 px (`--control-height-md`); the parent defines the width.
notasIA: Accepts all `<input>` props (`type`, `value`, `onChange`, `placeholder`, `disabled`…) and the `ref` points to the native element.
`error` is a string, not a boolean: pass the text when there is an error and `undefined` when there is none; the `description` stays visible along with the error.
There are no size variations or room for an icon or button inside the field: for that there are `password-field`, `search-field`, and `money-input`.

quandoUsar: Comments, messages, and notes where people are cited with `@` or channels with `#` and you need to know who was mentioned.
When the text will be stored or generate notifications: the value carries the plain text and `mentions` with `id` and positions, and `serializeMentions` converts it to `<@id>` and `<#id>`.
Quick-send boxes: with `submitOnEnter`, `Enter` calls `onSubmit` and `Shift + Enter` breaks the line.
quandoEvitar: Use `textarea` when the text has no mentions.
Use `rich-text-editor` when you need formatting, like bold, lists, and headings.
Use `prompt-input` for an assistant's message box, with attachments and a send button.

teclado.acao: With suggestions open, move the highlight, wrapping around at the ends.
With suggestions open, insert the highlighted one as a mention.
Closes the suggestions without erasing what was typed.
Next to a mention, erase the whole token at once.
Jump over a mention: the cursor never stops inside it.
With `submitOnEnter`, breaks the line, while `Enter` alone sends.

acessibilidade: The box is a `<textarea>` with `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-activedescendant`; the suggestions are a `role="listbox"`, and focus never leaves the text.
There is no built-in visible label: pass `aria-label`, or an `id` with your own `<label>` pointing to it.
An `aria-live` region announces how many people or channels match, but in fixed English (`3 people`, `No matches`), as are the list names.
movimento: The box height follows the text with a spring, between `minRows` and `maxRows`; beyond that the content scrolls.
Suggestions appear next to the `@` or `#` character, the highlight slides between rows, and the panel height follows the number of results.
With “reduce motion” on, heights and highlight change instantly and the panel only fades.
responsivo: Takes 100% of the width; the suggestions panel is 272 px, stays clamped within the box width and, with `placement="auto"`, opens upward when there are less than 300 px free below.
desempenho: The text is drawn by a mirror layer redone on every key, and the search scans all of `people` or `channels` to show at most `maxSuggestions` (default 6); avatars use `loading="lazy"`.
notasIA: The value is `{ text, mentions }`, not a string: use `value` + `onChange` or `defaultValue`, and read `mentions` (`kind`, `id`, `label`, `start`, `end`) when saving.
Pass `people` to enable `@` and `channels` to enable `#`; without the list, the matching trigger is turned off.
The `ref` exposes `focus()`, `insert(texto)`, `openSuggestions(kind)`, and `clear()`: useful for an “@” button in the toolbar and for clearing the box after sending.

quandoUsar: Payment, invoice, transfer, or budget values that go to the server as an integer in cents, with no floating-point rounding.
Forms with more than one currency: the menu switches the currency keeping the typed number, and symbol and decimal places follow; in yen, which has no cents, the fraction drops.
Top-ups, tips, and donations where round values do the job: the `quickAdd` chips add +10, +50, and +100 and the arrows advance one unit at a time.
quandoEvitar: Use `number-field` for values that can be negative, like a balance adjustment, with a negative `min` and `prefix`: this field only accepts digits and the decimal separator.
Use `range-histogram-slider` to choose a price range in a filter.
When the value needs more places than the currency, like an exchange rate: decimal places follow the currency (two in the real, none in the yen) and typing beyond them is rejected.

teclado.acao: In the field, add or subtract `step` (by default, one currency unit); with `Shift`, ten times that.
Add or subtract ten times the `step`.
In the field, fills in the missing decimal places, like `12` becoming `12.00`.
On a thousands separator, erase the neighboring digit instead of stopping at the separator.
On the currency button, `↓` and `↑` open the menu; in it, they move the highlight, stopping at the ends, and letters search by currency code or name.
In the menu, choose the highlighted currency; `Esc` closes and returns focus to the button, and `Tab` closes and moves on.

acessibilidade: The field is a text `<input>` with `role="spinbutton"`, `aria-valuenow` in whole units, and `aria-valuetext` with the formatted value; `label` is required and `hideLabel` leaves it for screen readers only.

Allowed range, `description`, and error go into `aria-describedby` and the error goes out in a `role="alert"`; a `role="status"` region announces the new value after a chip or an arrow and the limit that refused the change.
The currency menu is a `role="listbox"` with `aria-activedescendant`; currency names follow `locale`, but `Quick add`, `Add …`, `Currency`, `Maximum is …`, and the range are fixed in English.
movimento: Digits roll in the direction of the change when the value comes from a chip, an arrow, or outside; while typing the swap is immediate, so the cursor is not delayed.
The missing cents stay dimmed in place, so the width does not change when completing the value; a long value shrinks to fit instead of scrolling, and the symbol rolls when the currency changes.
At the limit, the value gives a sideways jolt and returns with a spring while the range flashes in a warning tone; with “reduce motion” on, there is no jolt or rolling and the digits only fade.
responsivo: Takes the container width with a 76 px height (`--money-input-height`); up to 420 px of screen the digits get smaller, and a value that does not fit shrinks instead of scrolling.
The currency menu opens below the field, right-aligned, with `min(256px, 100vw - 2rem)` and no portal: avoid ancestors with `overflow: hidden`.
notasIA: The value is an integer in minor units: R$ 12.50 is `1250`, ¥ 1250 is `1250`, and `null` is empty; `min`, `max`, and `step` are also in minor units, but `quickAdd` is in whole units.
To fix the currency, pass `currency` (or `defaultCurrency`) and `currencies` with only that code; with `currencies={["BRL"]}` alone, the field stays on the `USD` default.
`max` rejects typing right away, but `min` is only checked when the field loses focus; `error` replaces that message, `locale="pt-BR"` swaps the separators, and `name` sends the minor units.

quandoUsar: Compact property selectors in bars and panels, like owner, status, or priority, where the trigger takes only the width of the chosen label.
Options that need an icon or avatar and a detail on the right (`icon`, `meta`), split into groups with a heading.
Lists of up to a few hundred options: above eight, a search field takes the trigger's place on open (`searchable="auto"`), and on smaller ones there is search by letter.
quandoEvitar: Use `select` in forms with aligned fields: here the trigger changes width with the chosen label, and there is no `description` or error state.
Use `multi-select` when the person can choose several values.
Use `combobox` when typing is the main path and the field should look like a text field from the start.

teclado.acao: With the list closed, open it with the highlight on the chosen option, or on the first; a letter also opens it, already filtering the search by it or, without search, landing on the option that starts with it.
With the list open, move the highlight one option, stopping at the ends; without a search field, letters go to the next option with that initial.
Move the highlight eight options.
Take the highlight to the first or last enabled option, opening the list if needed; in the search field with text, they move the cursor.
With the list open, choose the highlighted option and return focus to the trigger; in the search field only `Enter` chooses, and `Alt + ↑` also works.
Closes without changing the choice and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` also closes and moves on to the next control.

acessibilidade: The trigger is a `<button role="combobox">` tied to the visible `label`, with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-activedescendant`: without search, focus stays on it while the highlight moves through the list.

With search, focus goes to the field, which takes on the `combobox` role, and a `role="status"` region announces how many options match; groups are `role="group"` and options have `aria-selected` and `aria-disabled`.
`placeholder` and `searchPlaceholder` change the empty texts, but the search name (`Search …`), the close button name (`Close …`), the count, and the no-results notice are fixed in English.
movimento: The trigger itself grows into the list: width, height, and corners follow a spring, and the options appear just behind the edge; on close, the surface shrinks back.
A highlight slides between options and, on choosing, the label leaves the list and flies to the trigger, which fits its width to the new text with a spring.
With “reduce motion” on, sizes and highlight change instantly and the value only fades, without the label's flight.
responsivo: Closed, the trigger has the width of the chosen label, up to `min(20rem, 100vw - 2rem)`; open, the surface uses `panelWidth` (default 272 px), never less than the trigger nor more than `100vw - 2rem`.
The list scrolls above `maxListHeight` (default 296 px) and the surface grows over the page from the `align` edge, with no portal: an ancestor with `overflow: hidden` clips it.
desempenho: All options stay mounted even with the list closed (hidden and `inert`) and there is no virtualization: the component itself is meant for up to a few hundred options.
notasIA: `items` mixes options `{ value, label, icon?, meta?, keywords?, disabled? }` and groups `{ label, options }`; use `value` + `onValueChange(value, option)` or `defaultValue`, with `null` for nothing chosen.
`searchable` defaults to `"auto"` and turns on search above eight options; pass `true` or `false` to fix it. The search looks at `label`, `meta`, and `keywords`.
`icon` accepts a 20 px node, like an `` avatar or an icon, and also appears on the trigger; `hideLabel` hides the visible label and `name` sends the value in a hidden field.

quandoUsar: Choosing several values from a short list inside a form, like teams, categories, or permissions.
When the field needs to stay short: only the first `maxVisible` chosen appear as chips and the rest becomes a `+N` counter.
When clearing everything at once is common: the clear button appears as soon as something is chosen.
quandoEvitar: Use `chip-group` when there are few options and all should stay in view, without opening a menu.
Use `tag-input` when the values are typed by the person, not chosen from a list.
For long lists: the menu shows all the options at once, with no search and no scrolling of its own.

teclado.acao: On the trigger, open the list and move the highlight through the enabled options, wrapping around at the ends.
With an option highlighted, checks or unchecks it without closing the list; with no highlight, opens or closes the list.
On the trigger, opens or closes the list.
With focus on the trigger, closes the list.
Moves through the clear button and each option, which `Enter` or `Space` check; leaving with `Tab` does not close the list.

acessibilidade: The trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and `aria-expanded`, named by the visible `label` and by the list of what was chosen, written out in full only for the screen reader.

The list is a `role="listbox"` with `aria-multiselectable` and options with `aria-selected`, but the highlight moved by the arrows is not announced, because the trigger does not use `aria-activedescendant`.
`description` appears under the field with no `aria-describedby` link, and the clear button has a fixed English name (`Clear selections`).
movimento: Each chosen chip opens its own space with a spring and grows from a slight blur, carrying its neighbors along; on exit, the space closes.
The `+N` counter rolls up when it increases and down when it decreases, and each option's checkmark draws itself on check and retracts on uncheck.
With “reduce motion” on, chips, counter, checkmarks, and menu only fade.
responsivo: Takes the container width; each chip is cut at 9rem with an ellipsis, and the menu opens below with the field's width, with no portal and no maximum height.
notasIA: Controlled with `value` + `onValueChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`; the array keeps the order in which the options were checked, and the chips follow that order.

Choosing does not close the menu, which is made for checking several options in a row: it closes with a click outside or on the trigger, with `Space` or `Esc` on the trigger, or on clearing everything.
There is no `name` prop: in a native form, generate the `<input type="hidden">` from `value`; `maxVisible` (default 2) defines how many chips appear before the `+N`.

quandoUsar: Bounded numbers the person can both type and adjust step by step: seats, quantity, price per unit.
Values with a unit that follows the number, like “1 seat” and “2 seats”: `prefix` and `suffix` accept text or a function of the value.
Property panels where dragging is faster than clicking: with `scrub`, dragging the label sideways changes one step every 6 px.
quandoEvitar: Use `adaptive-stepper` for small counters that need no typing and should keep a fixed width.
Use `money-input` for money, with currency, cents, and output in minor units.
Use `scrub-input` in compact editors that need units, math in the field itself, and fine steps with `Alt`.

teclado.acao: Add or subtract `step`; holding repeats and accelerates, and with `Shift` the step becomes `largeStep`.
Add or subtract `largeStep` (by default, ten steps).
Go to `min` or to `max` (`End` only when `max` was defined); while typing, they move the cursor.
Applies the typed value, adjusted to the step and limits; with no typing, selects the number.
While typing, discards the text and returns to the value from before the edit.
Moves through the minus button, the number, and the plus button; on the buttons, `Enter` and `Space` take one step.

acessibilidade: The number is an `<input>` with `role="spinbutton"` tied to the visible `label`, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuetext` already including `prefix` and `suffix`, and the limits when defined.
The buttons stay in the tab order and, at the limit, get `aria-disabled` without losing focus; their names are `Decrease …` and `Increase …`, in English.

An `aria-live` region announces the value after a click on the buttons or a drag of the label, and the limit reached; the visible `Max …`/`Min …` note changes with `limitHint` or disappears with `false`.
movimento: Each digit turns like an odometer in the direction of the change, wrapping from 9 to 0, and the columns open or close the width when the number gains or loses a digit.
At the limit, the value pushes toward it and returns with a spring, a little more with each consecutive attempt; the refused button's icon shakes and a note with the limit appears next to the label.
With “reduce motion” on, nothing moves: digits only fade and pushing against a limit only tints the number for a moment.
responsivo: The width comes from `--number-field-width` (196 px; 164 in `sm` and 228 in `lg`), capped at 100% of the container, and the height follows `size`: 36, 44, or 50 px.
desempenho: Each digit mounts a wheel with the ten numerals, each with its own animated styles: in a table with dozens of fields, prefer a simple field like `input`.
notasIA: Controlled with `value` + `onValueChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultValue` (default `0`); since `min` is also `0` by default, pass a negative `min` to accept values below zero.
A value typed within the limits and the step already calls `onValueChange` while typing; the rest is adjusted on confirming or leaving the field, and decimal places follow those of `step`.
Pass `locale="pt-BR"` for decimal comma and thousands period and `formatOptions` for places or grouping; there is no `name` prop, so send the value from your state.

quandoUsar: A password at login or password change, when the person wants to check what they typed before sending.
Other typed secrets, like an API key, by replacing the button names with `messages`.
quandoEvitar: Use `password-strength` when the person is creating a password and needs to see the requirements and strength while typing.
Use `otp-input` for six-digit verification codes.

teclado.acao: Moves focus from the field to the eye button.
On the eye button, show or hide the password.

acessibilidade: `label` becomes a `<label>` tied to the field, and `description` goes into `aria-describedby` along with whatever you pass in that prop.
The eye button has `aria-pressed` and a name that toggles between `Show password` and `Hide password`; translate with `messages={{ showPassword, hidePassword }}`.
There is no error prop: pass `aria-invalid` for the border to turn red and tie your message via `aria-describedby`.
movimento: When showing the password, a stroke draws over the eye, cutting the outline from below, and retracts on hiding, instead of swapping one icon for the other.
The swap between dots and letters appears with a brief fade and blur from the first click, and the help line opens its own height with a spring.
With “reduce motion” on, the stroke swaps instantly, the text does not fade, and the button does not shrink when pressed.
notasIA: Accepts `<input>` props except `type` (`value`, `onChange`, `name`, `autoComplete`…) and the `ref` points to the field; use `autoComplete="current-password"` at login and `"new-password"` at signup.
Showing or hiding is internal state: there is no prop to control it or to know whether the password is visible.
